summary: M.S. Computer Engineering candidate at RIT (May 2026) with firmware and embedded systems experience across STM32 Cortex-M4, FreeRTOS, and bare-metal C. Built real-time microcontroller systems with timer-driven ADC, interrupt-driven UART/I2C drivers, and RTOS task coordination across internship and capstone projects.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi Pico and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands over a custom firmware stack.
Implemented a tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding with software calibration to eliminate sensor jitter across use cases.
Produced full technical documentation and BOM for a Mixed Reality headset concept using AI-based real-time chroma keying.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member team across national-level competitions, owning PCB fabrication, embedded hardware integration, and firmware debugging end-to-end.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a Python GUI with PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization; maintained documentation and version control via GitLab.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed STM32 Cortex-M4 peripherals in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver from scratch.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Deployed YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson for real-time object tracking; routed control commands to STM32 over UART with interrupt-driven multi-servo PWM control.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensor for distance visualization on OLED.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link IK in embedded C++ on Arduino; drove 5 servos with range-gated contact detection via dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over I2C mux.
Resolved 11 hardware/firmware integration failures (servo crosstalk, sensor false-positives); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
1st Prize, Poster Presentation — 2D and 3D Image Mosaicing, F.C.R.I.T. (2024)
